question.worked_solution:
Since the logarithms on both sides of the equation have the same base, we can equate the arguments. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(-x+4) \\ {x}^{2}-2 & =-x+4 \\ {x}^{2}+x-6 & =0 \\ (x+3)(x-2) & =0 \\ x & =-3,2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now check for extraneous solutions by substituting back into the original equation:

- Substituting $x=-3$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(-x+4) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡((-3)^{2}-2) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(-(-3)+4) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(7).\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=-3$ is a valid solution.

- Substituting $x=2$ back into the original equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-2) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(-x+4) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡((2)^{2}-2) & \overset{?}{=}\operatorname{ln}⁡(-(2)+4) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(2).\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x=2$ is a valid solution.

Therefore, the correct answer is $x=-3,2.$
